newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firms as BOT widens controls.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firms as BOT widens controls.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed in offshore markets on Wednesday as the dollar hit lows not seen in almost seven months against the yen and the central Bank of Thailand (BOT) tightened its grip on speculators, dealers said.

The baht was quoted at 23.850/23.900 to the dollar at 0440 GMT in the offshore market compared with 24.050/24.250 late on Tuesday. It was at 25.720/25.730 in the domestic market against 25.743/25.753 late on Tuesday.
The BOT set the mid-rate at 25.71 per dollar versus 25.72 on Tuesday.
"The market is still very short of baht so there will be selling interest on any uptick in the dollar/baht," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
She said the central bank's latest move to cut off baht supply to foreigners through the stock market was also causing more selling of dollars for baht.
The BOT asked bank custodians on Tuesday not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks sought by foreigners in a move to plug loopholes for foreigners to raise offshore baht.
The central bank also said non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must be paid only in foreign currencies and the payment be made promptly to specific investors.

Signs that the capital controls imposed by Thai authorities since the baht came under speculative assault in mid-May were going to stay in place for some time yet fuelled jitters in the market, dealers said.

Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday that current capital control measures introduced by the authorities to curb speculation in the baht were temporary, but more permanent ones would be announced soon.
A senior BOT official told Reuters the central bank was working on measures to institutionalise the current controls to fend off future speculation, but did not provide a time frame.
In Indonesia, the rupiah showed a firmer bias amid tight money market liquidity but dealers said activity was confined to a narrow range.
"Trading is better than Tuesday but volume remains low. In fact the general view hasn't changed yet, with offshore slightly long in rupiah forwards," a Singapore bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,427.50/28.00 at 0440 GMT against an opening of 2,428.0/29.0.
Dealers said trade was driven by relatively tight liquidity, keeping the dollar under pressure. Overnight money was traded at 13.0/14.0 percent.
Dealers were mixed over the impact of the weakening dollar against the yen on dollar/rupiah rates.

A U.S. bank dealer said some seemed to attribute the rupiah's strength to the fall in dollar/yen but others were looking at the potential impact on Indonesia's budget, which would be negative if the yen continued to rise.
Indonesia has set a dollar/yen exchange rate of 110 for its 1997/98 budget starting April.
The dollar slipped to 110.97 yen in early Tokyo trade, its lowest level since November 20, 1996, on concerns about Japan's growing trade surplus.
The Malaysian ringgit recovered from its overnight lows as exporters sold the dollar near its highs.
"Exporters are selling the dollar around 2.5150 and this is capping the dollar/ringgit's rise," a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur said.
Strong dollar buying by two U.S. hedge funds at the 2.5100 level pushed the dollar/ringgit to a high of 2.5160 in thin overseas markets on Tuesday.
Dealers said many funds were still short dollars and were looking to cover their positions.
Across the border, the Singapore dollar's rise was thwarted by local bank buying of the U.S. dollar, raising fears of central bank intervention.

"Dollar/Sing will be under pressure but I think the local banks are around at the 1.4180 level. I would favour selling any rallies to 1.4220/30 or above to see an eventual test of the low end of 1.4100," said a dealer.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore typically intervenes in forex markets through major local banks to stem sharp rises in the local dollar.
